onboarding.first-step: Let's start a quick guide to help you effectively use our application. This will introduce you to the key features that will make your work easier. Let's begin!
onboarding.second-step: To use the assistant and allow others access to documents, you must belong to an 'organization'. This is the first important step.
onboarding.third-step: In the organization registration form, you'll find three fields, with only the organization name being required.
onboarding.fourth-step: Once the form is completed, you can confirm the organization setup to proceed.
onboarding.fifth-step: After creating an organization, new tabs will appear in the application. Now, let's go to the assistant management section.
onboarding.sixth-step: In this section, you have the option to customize your assistant to suit your needs. For now, fill in only the 'OpenAI API Key' field to activate the assistant.
onboarding.seventh-step: The final but crucial step is to provide knowledge to the assistant. You have two options to do this.
onboarding.eighth-step: If you do not have epub or markdown documents, use the editor to create a document adapted to the assistant or paste prepared content.
onboarding.ninth-step: If you have files in the previously mentioned formats, you can simply upload them from your device.

pii-policy.label: PII Masking Policy
pii-policy.none-description: No masking. Use for public documents, regulations, FAQs.
pii-policy.toxic-only-description: Masks PESEL, ID card, IBAN, credit cards. Keeps names, emails, phone numbers.
pii-policy.strict-description: Also masks names, emails, phone numbers, locations. Use for HR, contracts.
pii-policy.inline-edit-tooltip: Policy saved. Click "Apply policy" to re-process the document with the new masking settings.
pii-policy.reembed-success: Document will be re-processed with the new policy
pii-policy.info-page-subtitle: Learn how Ragen protects personal data in your documents.
pii-policy.none-examples: Terms of service, FAQ, product documentation, privacy policies
pii-policy.toxic-only-masks: PESEL, ID card, IBAN, credit cards — does not mask emails, phone numbers, names
pii-policy.toxic-only-examples: Most business documents, contracts with contact data
pii-policy.strict-masks: Everything: PESEL, ID, IBAN, plus emails, phone numbers, names, locations
pii-policy.strict-examples: HR documents, payroll, contracts with lists of individuals
pii-policy.data-local-processing: Documents are analyzed by Presidio running within Ragen infrastructure. Data is not sent to external providers during masking.
pii-policy.data-vector-store: In destructive mode, only masked text is stored in the vector database — original values (e.g. PESEL) are never persisted. In dual-content mode, an AES-256-GCM encrypted original is stored alongside the masked version, accessible only to the AI model.
pii-policy.data-policy-change: Changing the policy on a folder or file requires re-processing the documents. This can be done from the folder edit dialog.
pii-policy.data-isolation: All documents are accessible only within your organization.
pii-policy.dual-content-notice: Your organization uses dual-content ingestion mode. The AI assistant always has access to the original unmasked data regardless of the masking policy selected below.
pii-policy.ingestion-mode-description: Controls what happens to documents after upload. Applies to new files only — previously processed documents are not affected.
pii-policy.ingestion-mode-destructive-description: Sensitive data is permanently removed before storage. The original is irreversibly replaced with a masked version — nothing sensitive leaves the masking step. Changing this setting requires re-processing your documents.
pii-policy.ingestion-mode-dual-content-description: Sensitive data is masked in the visible content, but an encrypted original is retained in the background — this allows the AI assistant to give more accurate answers. Original data passes through the search infrastructure. Enable only if your security policy permits it.

setup.database-unreachable-intro: DATABASE_URL is set, but connecting failed. Check that Postgres is running and that the database exists.

findings.database: Nothing works without a database — not even signing in.
findings.auth-secret: Sessions are signed with this. Left unset, every restart signs everyone out.
findings.secret-key: Encrypts organization API keys at rest. Saving a key fails without it.
findings.llm-gateway: Every chat and embedding call goes through the LiteLLM proxy. Chat returns an error until it is reachable.
findings.default-model: New conversations have no model to fall back on when the organization has not picked one.
findings.vector-store: Document retrieval falls back to a local Qdrant. Set this explicitly once Qdrant runs anywhere else.
findings.temporal: Uploaded documents are never parsed or embedded — the ingest workflow has nowhere to run.
findings.mail: No mail transport is configured, so verification links, magic links and invitations are only written to the log. Set up Resend or an SMTP server to deliver them.
findings.app-url: Links in emails and in the embeddable chat widget need an absolute origin. Either variable works; BETTER_AUTH_URL is read at runtime, NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL is baked in at build time.
findings.target-env: Names the deployment. Left unset, traces and metrics report no environment, and email links have no local fallback to fall back to.
findings.message-encryption: Thread messages are stored as plaintext. Fine locally; set one of these before real conversations go in.
findings.embeddings-dimension-mismatch: EMBEDDINGS_MODEL={model} produces {expected}-dimensional vectors, but VECTOR_SIZE is {configured}. Qdrant rejects every upsert, so no document ever becomes searchable.
findings.object-storage-credentials: STORAGE_PROVIDER=s3 is set, but some of its configuration is missing. Uploads and downloads fail until these are set — use the S3_ prefix (S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID, S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, S3_REGION), not AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY / AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, which are reserved for AWS Bedrock and AWS KMS.
